headline: LSU's Ground Game Grinds Down Tennessee in Defensive Struggle
body: LSU's offense never sparkled on Saturday, but it didn't need to. Tim Ferguson carved out 50 yards on 12 carries and punched in two touchdowns, anchoring a dominant ground attack that controlled the line of scrimmage and the clock. Tennessee's defense had no answer for the relentless run game, and with Nussmeier managing rather than forcing the issue through the air, LSU's coaching room kept the chains moving and the scoreboard ticking in their favor.

The numbers tell the story of a program that executed its identity. LSU out-gained Tennessee 329 to 200 and held the ball long enough to wear down a Volunteer defense that couldn't generate consistent stops. Tennessee's Bishop ran hard for 91 yards and found the end zone once, but it amounted to damage control. MacIntyre and the passing game never found rhythm, and the offense sputtered whenever it tried to keep pace.

Where LSU's defense truly separated itself was in protecting the football. A single fumble lost versus Tennessee's unforced turnover proved decisive in a game decided by 10 points. Ross sacked Nussmeier twice for Tennessee and showed up when he could, but his effort came too late in a contest where field position and time of possession already favored the visiting team.
turningPoint: Ferguson's second touchdown run late in the third quarter effectively put the game out of reach, as Tennessee's offense had shown no ability to match LSU's sustained drives.

unsungHero.name: Stafford
unsungHero.why: His five tackles and sack went largely unheralded because Ferguson's two touchdown runs captured all the attention, but Stafford's work in containing Tennessee's ground game and disrupting MacIntyre's timing was foundational to the shutout performance in the second half.
